quoted_positive_example:
Warehouse packing schedule handbook — record 1

Procedure. Use all six whole packing machines within the stated bay limits. Choose the schedule that minimizes unfinished orders, then the largest proportional backlog, then apply the alphabetical tie-break.

Operational state. {"bays": {"A": {"machine_limit": 4, "open_orders": 50, "orders_per_machine": 10}, "B": {"machine_limit": 4, "open_orders": 60, "orders_per_machine": 10}, "C": {"machine_limit": 4, "open_orders": 28, "orders_per_machine": 10}}, "machine_budget": 6}

Valid schedule. {"A": 2, "B": 3, "C": 1}
Status label. VALID

Operational explanation. Assigning packing machines where they finish the most pending orders reduces the total remaining backlog. For this state, the schedule follows all machine limits, uses the complete machine budget, and applies the throughput objective and tie-break.

Practice. Calculate consequences from the displayed figures, give the valid schedule, and explain how the schedule advances order completion under the procedure. Record code WH-001.
